articles.title: Fencing Lessons - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Fencing Lessons Is a Side Quest in Novigrad with suggested level 12. This quest becomes available after Broken Flowers, if you agree to give Rosa more lessons,
articles.body:
Fencing Lessons Is a Side Quest in Novigrad with suggested level 12. This quest becomes available after Broken Flowers , if you agree to give Rosa more lessons, and it's a rather straightforward one in comparison to other Novigrad Side Quests.

To help you complete the Side Quest quickly, here's IGN's complete guide to Fencing Lessons, including the various options you'll have on offer when dealing with the duo of thugs at the very end.

You'll need to finish Broken Flowers before you can start this Side Quest. Speaking to Rosa during Broken Flowers will reveal that she wants fencing lessons, and if you agree, you'll be invited back to her estate the following day.

At Rosa's home, you'll be told that she's not actually home, and is instead on a walk with her bodyguard in the city. You'll need to head out and find her in the south east area of the city, near the water.

Rosa will request to fight with real swords, sending her bodyguard away. As you might imagine, there isn't much of a threat here, and you'll be able to beat her quickly with simple strikes.

After bringing Rosa's health down a significant amount, she'll order Geralt to turn around so she can readjust her corset. After complying, Geralt will turn back around to see that Rosa has slipped away.

Use your Witcher Senses to track Rosa to the Seven Cats Inn.

You will find two thugs harassing Rosa in the Inn. You'll be able to decide how you want to deal with them. You can use Axii, pay them off, or simply kill them. This won't change your final Side Quest reward.

When the thugs have been dealt with, a very unhappy Rosa will go home, wrapping up the Side Quest.

There isn't much of a reward on offer here; you'll be able to nab 25 x experience when you wrap up this Side Quest.

articles.title: Contract: The White Lady - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Contract: The White Lady is a Novigrad Side Quest. It has a suggested level of 16, and has a heavy, emotional story at its core. Some Side Quests simply
articles.body:
Contract: The White Lady is a Novigrad Side Quest . It has a suggested level of 16, and has a heavy, emotional story at its core. Some Side Quests simply require you to kill a monster and move on -- this one features a monster, but there's more to it than meets the eye.

To help you prepare for the combat encounter and complete the Side Quest, here's IGN's complete guide to Contract: The White Lady, including where to start the Contract and what you'll need to bring.

This Side Quest can be started by picking up the notice paper reading Contract: The White Lady off the notice board in the refugee district of the outskirts of Novigrad.

The Contract will guide you to a widow named Helma, who will tell you more about the monster that's plaguing the townsfolk -- it's some kind of Wraith, apparently. She can be found to the south of the area.

Four townspeople went to defeat the Wraith, but when you arrive at the designated crime scene and investigate using your Witcher Senses, you'll only see three bodies.

After examining the bodies, Geralt will determine that The White Lady is a Noonwraith .

Near the dead bodies, there will be some tracks leading away from the other bodies. Use your Witcher Senses and follow the tracks. The tracks lead to a broken tower and you will be led, in turn, to the cellar via a blood trail.

Head back to Helma to find something to draw the Noonwraith out. After talking to the widow, she will give you a dagger. Seemingly, the Noonwraith is a woman who took her life to avoid an arranged marriage, and the dagger was a betrothal gift.

Head back to the campsite which is near the dead bodies. Be sure to use your Specter Oil beforehand if you haven't already, and wait until it's daytime for the Noonwraith to appear if it isn't already. Throw the dagger into the fire when you're ready to fight.

Much like other Wraiths in the game, this Noonwraith is vulnerable to both Specter Oil and Yrden. You'll need to use Yrden to make sure that the beast is strikable, and dodge her attacks in the meanwhile.

When the Noonwraith falls, loot the body to claim a Noonwraith Trophy and the Silver Sword Deithwen, then head back to the quest-giver to turn in the Side Quest and claim your final reward.

Turning in this Side Quest will net you your negotiated fee, along with 260 x experience.

articles.title: Contract: The Oxenfurt Drunk - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Contract: The Oxenfurt Drunk is a Novigrad Side Quest with a suggested level of 26. It's a murder mystery, with two key leads for Geralt to follow in
articles.body:
Contract: The Oxenfurt Drunk is a Novigrad Side Quest with a suggested level of 26. It's a murder mystery, with two key leads for Geralt to follow in order to solve the crime and get to the bottom of what's causing the attacks in Oxenfurt.

Here's IGN's complete guide to Contract: The Oxenfurt Drunk, including where to start the Side Quest and how to beat the combat encounter at the end.

To begin this Side Quest, head to Oxenfurt in the north of Velen, and look for the paper reading "Contract: Monster in Oxenfurt" as a starting point.

You'll need to find a character named Nikolas at the docks in Oxenfurt to learn more about the so-called monster, and the bodies that've been turning up in the gutter.

There are two leads for Geralt to follow with this Contract. You can speak to the witness, a lady who survived the attack, and speak to the medic caring for the bodies to examine them.

Talking to the witness, she sounds like a drunk lunatic, and she gets mad. Talking to the medic, he gets anxious about Geralt investigating the bodies. Examining the bodies, Geralt determines its a Vampire .

Head to where the monster was seen, and investigate using your Witcher senses. You'll discover a bracelet. Head back to the tavern, and get drunk to bait the Katakan. After getting drunk, Geralt will roam the streets singing drunk songs.

Eventually the Katakan emerges, and you will have to fight him, whilst drunk. Don't burn any combat items in this initial engagement, as you only need to take off a fourth of his health before he runs away -- focus on heavy attacks and dodging.

Follow the Katakan's trail using your Witcher Senses. The trail will lead to a house, which you can enter via a ladder. Finish off the Katakan, focusing on your movement in the enclosed area and watching for quick strikes. Don't be afraid to use additional items like Bombs here, either.

When you've beaten the beast, loot the corpse for a Katakan Trophy, the Deardgeith sword, a key to let you out of the locked house, and the Katakan Mutagen.

Return to the quest giver for your reward and to wrap up the Side Quest.

You'll receive your negotiated amount of money when turning in this Contract, along with 300 x experience, making it a worthwhile Contract to take on.

articles.title: Merchandise - A Court of Thorns and Roses Guide - IGN
articles.summary: A Court of Thorns and Roses (also known as ACOTAR) is a popular romantasy series that became a viral hit on #BookTok on TikTok. While an ACOTAR TV series was
articles.body:
A Court of Thorns and Roses (also known as ACOTAR) is a popular romantasy series that became a viral hit on #BookTok on TikTok. While an ACOTAR TV series was in the works at Hulu, it was scrapped in February 2025 . Still, two new books were announced by author Sarah J. Maas in March 2026 and are set to release in October 2026 and January 2027. Even without the TV adaptation, the series is moving beyond the pages of the book, expanding to tabletop games , jewelry, Funko Pop figures, and more.

The series’ publisher, Bloomsbury, has its own gift guide for ACOTAR and Maas’ other series, Throne of Glass and Crescent City, which are all connected via a multiverse (Maasverse). Additional official merchandise for ACOTAR can be found from sites, including Amazon, Target, and other online bookstores .

A Court of Thorns and Roses - Fate & Favor Board Game

An original strategy board game based on the books , called Fate & Favor, is available now. In the game, you play as either the High Lord or Lady of one of the seven Courts of Prythian as you forge alliances and fight for power. It’s full of familiar characters and scenes from the series, with event cards and shifting fate tokens, making things even more interesting. Created by true fans of ACOTAR, incredible detail is poured into everything from the gameplay to the artwork.

A Court of Thorn and Roses - Fate & Favor Booksellers Edition

A special “Bookseller Variant” with exclusive packaging at select bookstores can also be purchased.

Monopoly: A Court of Thorns and Roses Special Edition Board Game

Monopoly: A Court of Thorns and Roses Edition Board Game for Adults

Similar to Fourth Wing , ACOTAR has a Monopoly Edition. There's a classic red option to match the paperback cover of the first book and an Amazon-exclusive green variant. Rather than your typical locations, like Park Place and Boardwalk, the board highlights memorable places from the series. Golden tokens with items from the book, including Feyre's Bow and The Suriel, also replace the typical game pieces. This Monopoly even offers manors and palaces over houses and hotels.

Priorities: A Court of Thorns and Roses Edition Game

Also from Hasbro is A Court of Thorns and Roses Edition of Priorities. It's a party game where players must work together to correctly rank ACOTAR themed cards.

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Collection: A Deck of Woulds or Rathers

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Collection: FAE or Fraud?

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Collection: Playing Card Set (Night Court Inner Circle)

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Fated Mates Pick-a-Stick: 50 Activities for Love & Romance

Several ACOTAR-themed card games are available or coming out, including a would-you-rather-type game, trivia, and a traditional deck of cards with characters from the Night Court. Another card-adjacent, adults-only activity provides prompts for a deeper connection with romantic partners.

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Collection: Seven Courts of the Faerie Realm 1000-Piece Puzzle

A Court of Thorns & Roses Starfall 250-Piece Puzzle

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Mystery Mini Puzzle: Feyre’s Portraits

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Collection: Greetings from Velaris 1000-Piece Puzzle

A Court of Thorns & Roses Walk Through The Rainbow 250 pcs Puzzle

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official A Tale of Fated Mates Rhysand and Feyre 1000-Piece Puzzle

A Court of Thorns & Roses Valkyrie Library Sleepover Keepsake 250 pcs Puzzle

A Court of Thorns and Roses Official Still Life with Dread Trove 1000-Piece Puzzle

You can find puzzles that depict iconic scenes, characters, places, and more from the series at Amazon, Target, and other sites. For something more challenging, grab the 1,000-piece options, and for a quicker activity, there are a few 250-piece puzzles. A fun mystery box puzzle also reveals one of six character portraits.

Twitter Logo Save Funko POP! Feyre Under The Mountain

Popular characters from ACOTAR are now Funko Pop figures . Feyre has three different versions: her painting dresser drawers, her when she heads under the mountain, and her with a bow and arrow. Other figures include Tamlin in both beast form and masked, a masked Lucien, Rhysand, Amarantha, and The Suriel.

Based on the figures, this collection’s focus appears to be on the first book in the series.

A Court of Thorns and Roses Book Charms Locket Necklace

A Court of Thorns and Roses Book Covers Charm Toggle Bracelet

A Court of Thorns and Roses Bat Boys Ring Set of 3

A Court of Thorns and Roses Feyre Archeron Linear Bracelet

Alex and Ani has its own A Court of Thorns and Roses jewelry collection . Everything from a locket with adorable miniatures of the first five books to a charm bracelet that showcases the symbols and color palette of each book cover is available. You can even pick up one of the three bracelets inspired by the Archeron sisters, Feyre, Nesta, and Elain or Bat Boys rings. The collection is massive and looks incredible.

Youtooz ACOTAR Feyre Collectible Plush Figure, 9-Inch

Cuddle up with your favorite ACOTAR characters, as Youtooz has its own lineup of limited-edition plushies. These 9-inch plush figures are stuffed with 100% PP cotton and feature tons of details, from magical tattoos to a glittering wardrobe. There are five characters available: Rhysand, Feyre, Cassian, Azriel, and Nesta. Some are only preorders with shipping expected to begin in November.

A Court Of Thorns And Roses Metallic Icons Hoodie

BrüMate x ACOTAR 40 fl oz Stainless Steel Era Flip 100% Leak-Proof Straw Tumbler - Starfall

A Court Of Thorns And Roses Feyre's Dresser Figural Vase

ACOTAR x Fine'ry Limited Edition - Night In Velaris Women's Perfume - No Prince Required

A Court Of Thorns And Roses Quote Night Court Tote Bag

A Court Of Thorns And Roses Icons Girls Knit Duster

A Court Of Thorns And Roses Click Pen Set

A Court Of Thorns And Roses Take Me To The Night Court T-Shirt

A Court Of Wings & Ruins Only You Decide What Breaks You Throw Blanket

A Court Of Thorns And Roses Post Stamp Notebook

Tons of ACOTAR clothing is available from sites like Amazon and Etsy, but the best and biggest selection of officially licensed apparel and more is at Hot Topic and Target . Both have other collectibles that make great gifts, like pens, blankets, vases, totes, perfume, lights, and more. All are themed after the first five books, featuring memorable quotes, items, and places from the series. A few products are also available on Amazon via third-party sellers.

A Court of Thorns and Roses Hardcover Box Set

A Court of Thorns and Roses Paperback Box Set

A Court of Thorns and Roses Collector's Edition

ACOTAR is a popular audiobook and eBook series, but hardcover and paperback editions are great if you’d also like a physical copy to look back at. All five books currently released are available in those two formats, and books six and seven, whose covers and titles were recently announced , have hardcover copies for preorder . There’s also a hardcover and paperback box set of the first five books. A Collector’s Edition of the first book, the series’ namesake, A Court of Thorns and Roses, can even be found on Amazon.

Play-Doh Blooms A Court of Thorns and Roses

Play-Doh is now for adults too and is getting in on the ACOTAR brand with a new Blooms kit. The new kit comes with everything you need to build a bouquet and will release on January 15.

articles.title: Dead by Daylight Developer Apologizes Again, Removes Free Items From TheBurntPeanut's Account
articles.summary: Behavior Interactive is currently under fire after one of its community staff allegedly went rogue and gifted controversial streamer TheBurntPeanut every in-game item in Dead by Daylight live on stream. The developer already apologized once on the secondary Dead by Daylight social media account, but this latest mea culpa, in an attempt to take full accountability, was posted on the full-fat account.
articles.body:
Behavior Interactive is currently under fire after one of its community staff allegedly went rogue and gifted controversial streamer TheBurntPeanut every in-game item in Dead by Daylight live on stream. The developer already apologized once on the secondary Dead by Daylight social media account, but this latest mea culpa, in an attempt to take full accountability, was posted on the full-fat account.

TheBurntPeanut gained popularity over the last year for playing extraction shooters like Arc Raiders, but his style of commentary is seen as edgy by some and problematic by others. Earlier this year, Fortnite was wrapped up in similar drama for collaborating with TheBurntPeanut due to accusations he’d allegedly used homophobic language online.

Dead by Daylight 10th Anniversary Broadcast Visual Overhaul Reveal - Screenshots

Dead by Daylight initially starts players with a small selection of playable characters, but they must spend in-game currency to earn the rest, while licensed characters cost around $5 in real money. Gifting TheBurntPeanut all the characters was taken as a betrayal by the community, which has many dedicated streamers who haven’t been gifted everything the game has to offer.

Not only was his alleged behavior never taken into account, but it sparked favoritism concerns considering it was the first time the streamer had shown an interest in Dead by Daylight. Initially, TheBurntPeanut offered to send the freebies back, concerned that it would cause drama. Responding to the online outrage, the studio reportedly sent support TheBurntPeanut's way, with the most infamous message saying, "WE CAN TAKE THE HEAT! THEY ARE YOURS TO KEEP!"

A video from seven months ago shows the streamer saying he doesn’t understand the game’s popularity. “No disrespect, but how the hell has a game where you fix four generators and then leave, rinse and repeat, been alive for ten years?” he said.

The streamer himself has since responded to the controversy, which bubbled away on social media between the weekend and today. “I just went on Twitter for a second and everyone’s pissed at us for getting free skins in Dead by Daylight,” TheBurntPeanut said in a recent video . “There’s one guy that’s submitted a refund, and in the refund reason box they go, ‘TheBurntPeanut collaboration and the response of the game’s communication team — I do not support racist transphobes.’

“I don’t think I’ve ever said anything about transgender people, I think, in the last two-and-a-half years of streaming. Have I ever said anything about transgender people?” He asked this question to another streamer, who replied: “I don’t think so, but there’s always time to start.” This made TheBurntPeanut start laughing. “Where are they getting this from?” he asked. He didn’t address the racism accusations.

Behavior Interactive’s new apology , posted on the main account, claimed that it will put in new approval processes to prevent community representatives from being able to choose who Dead by Daylight collaborates with without checks.

Explaining the initial decision to grant TheBurntPeanut an unlocked account, the latest apology claimed that the team saw a new streamer with a large audience playing the game and got excited at the prospect of reaching new players. But the decision to grant the account perks happened without any internal discussion.

“When collaborating with a new creator, we normally look thoroughly at their past content to determine whether they are representing the values of inclusion our community expects from us,” Behaviour explained. “In this case, this was not taken into proper consideration or discussed as a group.”

The studio also spoke about the infamous “WE CAN TAKE THE HEAT” message. “This message, along with some others in that session, showed a disregard for the context we were suddenly in and crossed the line of appropriate responses from our brand,” the statement continued. “That reply escalated the situation for us and for our community, especially our content creators on the frontlines of these conversations, and that’s unacceptable.”

According to the developer, the account bonuses have already been removed from TheBurntPeanut, and Behavior is rewriting its guidelines for interacting with creators and identifying potentially problematic collaborations. The studio is “taking appropriate action internally” to deal with the employee involved, but the details of this will remain confidential.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: What Does Sentinel Mean? Are Giant Robots Involved? The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Lore Explained
articles.summary: What does Sentinel mean? How is it connected to Skyrim? Are we getting giant robots? Here's a deep dive lore explainer on The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel.
articles.body:
The worst-kept secret in gaming has finally been confirmed: yes, The Elder Scrolls 6 has a title. It’s called Sentinel, and will take place in Hammerfell, the province of northwest Tamriel previously featured in Daggerfall and Elder Scrolls Online (also Arena, but anyone who says they played that recently is lying). The point is, more than any previous mainline entry in the Elder Scrolls series, Sentinel will be depicting a fairly well-trodden location. But given its geographical location and significance in The Lore, I think there’s a fairly good chance that TES 6 will feature two distinct elements: ships and giant robots. Stay with me on this.

So what is Sentinel? Well, it’s a city and kingdom – think New York, New York – on the southern shores of the Iliac Bay, the northern edge of Hammerfell province, stretching from the Alik'r Desert and coastal regions in the west to the Dragontail Mountains in the east.

It’s a hugely important maritime city in Tamrielic lore, being the founding settlement of the Redguards. Its geography and architecture are heavily inspired by North Africa and the Middle East: the city of Sentinel is often depicted almost like classical Baghdad, with its beautiful domed palace and spires in the centre, river canals lined with palm trees, and sandblasted common districts full of markets and street vendors. It is one of the preeminent locations of TheElder Scrolls 2: Daggerfall, second only perhaps to Daggerfall itself, its opposite number and historical rival across the water. Like Rome and Carthage squabbling over Sicily, Sentinel and Daggerfall’s shared past mostly pivots around a dispute over the island of Betony, a strategically significant fishing community off the coast of High Rock which used to be a protectorate of Sentinel until Daggerfall decided to sink their navy over it.

It’s a region rich with naval tradition, arguably with lots of parallels to the Mediterranean. The northern province of High Rock may be taken as a composite of Latin and Germanic Europe as a counterpart to Sentinel’s obvious riffs on the Arab-descended Moorish people who once colonised the Iberian Peninsula. Which is fitting, because if Elder Scrolls is anything, it’s extremely moreish.

What’s important is that the Iliac Bay is full of tiny islands. The lore is steeped in boat stuff. The Redguards themselves are a seafaring people in the same way that Bretons are a magic one, or that the Imperials are really good at accountancy: it’s at the heart of their culture, their DNA. Which, given that Sentinel is named for their home nation, would seem to track with the rumour from several billion years ago that The Elder Scrolls 6 would feature, or at least was once intended to feature, some sort of ship-based component. That could mean anything or nothing, of course, but if every Elder Scrolls game is to be its own proposition, then this would certainly be a defining trope for the new one. Skyrim had dragons. Oblivion had portals to hell. Morrowind had big mushrooms. Yum.

Beyond the bay itself, we have the fallen continent of Yokuda, where the Redguards originally hail from, and the large island nation of Stros M’Kai, the setting of Bethesda’s one-time experiment in doing a third-person adventure spin-off of the Elder Scrolls. The Elder Scrolls Adventures: Redguard wasn’t a huge success in itself, but it did teach the studio a great deal about the relationship between scale and hand-crafted detail that resulted in a massive difference in approach between Daggerfall and Morrowind. Where the former boasted a map twice the size of the UK, Morrowind crammed infinitely more intrigue into a region barely a full percentage of the size, brought the series to consoles, and subsequently made the studio a household name.

Bethesda would stick to this philosophy of staunchly hand-crafted worlds until Starfield, which depicted a thousand-planet galaxy of endless walking, pocked with procedurally generated identikit outposts and very little incentive to go off the laid-out path, which many would argue – myself included, and I like Starfield – betrayed a studio that had lost touch with its core appeal. But think of the parts of Starfield which are successful, at least as a proof of concept: a mobile home in the form of a starship, to which you can assign crew, and go adventuring with them. A hugely popular ship builder that simplified the process of pimping your ride down to a snap-together kitbash, that allowed for enormous creativity within a deceptively rigid framework.

It’s not a given that any of this will be relevant to Sentinel, or that if any of these systems carried over they would retain their complexity. But it does demonstrate that, if TES 6 were to think about this sort of direction, it’s hardly unprecedented at this point.

What’s also not unprecedented in Bethesda’s oeuvre is kaiju. Big bastards smashing the gaffe up. Some years before Fallout 3’s Liberty Prime made us all piss ourselves unintentionally, the end of Oblivion depicted daedric prince Mehrunes Dagon ransacking the Imperial City, and you’ll probably remember that he’s a big dude, so big that he could only be seen off by the literal embodiment of Akatosh as a nine-storey dragon. And yes, the dragons of Skyrim qualify: the entire game being built around the proposition of seeing off a veritable invasion of enormous, scaly bastards. And Morrowind before them was all about preventing Dagoth Ur from building a second Numidium with which to conquer the world: a gigantic Dwarven mech powered by the literal heart of a god, based on the schematics of a weapon of mass destruction that was once used by the city-state of Sentinel to conquer the rest of the region.

And there’s a whole other bunch of stuff that happened: if you want to know more, boot up Morrowind, or Oblivion, or Skyrim, and read an in-game book entitled The Warp in the West, which explains a convoluted collision of realities in which every rival faction got to use Numidium to get their preferred Daggerfall ending, making all of them canon at once. Which you might call a cop-out, but it certainly neatly solves the kinds of insurmountable issues that crop up when you try to respect all player choices.

The point is this: after the events of Daggerfall, Numidium is destroyed, and pieces of it are scattered all over Hammerfell and High Rock. Perhaps some of it sank to the bottom of the bay. Perhaps some of it is buried in the desert. The quote displayed at the end of the recent Sentinel teaser talks about the experience of Yazar, a Moth Priest, trying to interpret a prophecy from one of the Elder Scrolls and receiving only a faint image of some kind of terrible future. Or past. Or parallel present. “A future lost, a victory undone, sands of time scattered by fate”.

Like much of Elder Scrolls lore, it is esoteric and steeped in double-meaning. As a region at the heart of the Warp in the West, the ‘sands of time’ could well refer literally to the Alik'r Desert while caught in a time-warp. A ‘victory undone’ may refer to any number of conflicts referenced in the series’ history, but the most pertinent one would seem to be Sentinel’s “victory” at the end of Daggerfall, in which it became the capital of a vast coastal region as the various bickering city-states and territories were consolidated into the four currently standing kingdoms of the Iliac Bay, which, along with Sentinel, includes the Breton kingdoms of Daggerfall and Wayrest, and the Orcish kingdom of Orsinium.

To undo the victory could mean to scatter these territories back to their fragments. Or, it could refer to the events preceding the last Elder Scrolls game, Skyrim, where the empire of Tamriel finds itself in a precarious peace with the treacherous Aldmeri Dominion after decades of brutal war, following the treaty known as the White Gold Concordat. This stipulated, firstly, the criminalisation of Talos worship, which much of Skyrim’s civil war arc is concerned with. Secondly, the disbanding of the Blades, the emperor’s secret service. And lastly, the cession of southern Hammerfell to the High Elves. You can imagine this didn’t go down especially well with the Redguards of Sentinel, which is why they left the Empire shortly afterward.

It’s not a huge stretch to assume that Sentinel will continue the story of this conflict, with the Aldmeri Dominion an occupying army in regions of Hammerfell that the player may be tasked with liberating. Or, perhaps we will be enrolled in an effort to construct a weapon with which to decisively end the war. Say, a giant dwarven mech. Reassembling the pieces of Numidium left by the warp in the west would seem to be a classic motivation for RPG storytelling. And it would be especially fitting to use against the High Elves. Numidium itself is a construct of the ancient Dwarves that has been used in a number of pivotal wars. Most notably, it was used by the founding emperor Tiber Septim to bring the Aldmeri to heel on Summerset Isle: a weapon of mass destruction set loose onto the entire civilian population, an incident which is largely credited with inspiring the general disdain High Elves have for the human races, and the Imperials in particular.

Numidium is an offensive cultural trauma for the Aldmeri Dominion. It represents the moment when they lost their sovereignty to the Empire, a subjugation that would last right up until the end of the Oblivion Crisis. The colossal machine is depicted in the Wall of Alduin in Skyrim, a part of the Dragonborn prophecy that is concerned with the warping of time which, according to the UESP, is an effect that occurs along with every known use of Numidium in history.

But what could power such a construct, in a world of candlelight and shit dinners? Well, the literal heart of a God. In Morrowind, the player character thwarts the building of a second Numidium by destroying the Heart of Lorkhan, or the Heart of the Red Mountain, one of the most important objects in the entire Elder Scrolls universe, perhaps even more important than the manuscripts themselves.

Sentinel is rumoured to be, at long last, concerned with the origins of the titular scrolls: these objects of divine prophecy that have shown up throughout the series but have never been fully understood. They are cared for by the Moth Priests, a sect of blind scholars whose work in interpreting the scrolls robs them of their sight; such is the retina-searing power of creation they are believed to hold. They are said to be byproducts of the creation of the universe, fragments of time, space, and everything. Star stuff. God particles. The celestial parchment on which is written the underlying code of existence. And Lorkhan, the missing god whose heart is required to power Numidium, was there at their creation, having tricked the god Mundus into creating the Elder Scrolls universe in the first place.

The Elder Scrolls 6 is likely the culmination of an enormous tapestry of imagined history that goes right back to Daggerfall, and deeply involves every single Elder Scrolls protagonist thereafter. Tracing the Heart of Lorkhan and the pieces of Numidium through history until, perhaps, their final reassembly in the war against Sentinel and the Aldmeri Dominion. And where is Lorkhan said to have died? At the Adamantine Tower, on the island of Balferia in the Iliac Bay. Perhaps something remains of him there that we will have to recover. Maybe we’ll end up flying to one of the moons in a big dwarven rocket to recover one of Lorkhan’s toes. I don’t know. But I’d love to do it. The upshot? The Elder Scrolls 6 is going to be absolutely stacked to the gills with tidbits for sickos. And I can’t wait to play it in 2038.

articles.title: The Cat in the Hat Animated Adaptation Features Bill Hader as the Whimsical Dr. Seuss Character
articles.summary: The Cat in the Hat (2026) review: The whimsical Dr. Seuss character gets a good but not great animated feature film showcase.
articles.body:
The Cat in the Hat is in theaters on on November 6.

Having received a 2003 live-action adaptation that left much to be desired , the Cat in the Hat is back with a new feature film. This time, it’s in animated form, and fortunately the end result is a much better one.

With Mike Myers having starred in the live-action version, another group of filmmakers have once more turned to a Saturday Night Live alum, with Bill Hader now voicing the Cat. Dr. Seuss's beloved children's book is far too short to make for a feature-length story on its own, so things are rather drastically reinterpreted and expanded upon here, with writer-directors Erica Rivinoja (South Park, Borat Subsequent Moviefilm) and Alessandro Carloni (Kung Fu Panda 3) essentially just taking the basic idea of the fantastical Cat in the Hat appearing to children to encourage imagination and mischief.

The opening scenes feel somewhat similar to Monsters, Inc., establishing an entire imagination-based business of sorts with the Cat in the Hat as an employee. Other anthropomorphic animals work alongside him, all in the service of providing entertainment and encouragement to kids needing an imagination boost. Fortunately, the film doesn’t get too bogged down in the “company” scenario, mostly using it as a fun way to incorporate nods to the Seuss-y source material in the form of rhyming rules explained by staff members (voiced by the likes of Giancarlo Esposito, Bowen Yang, and Quinta Brunson), along with some visual depictions of the Cat in that Hat that also harken back to the book. From there, the story follows the Cat appearing to sister and brother Gabby (Xochitl Gomez) and Sebastian (Tiago Martinez), who are trying to deal with moving to a new city with their mother, Carmen (America Ferrera).

The Cat in the Hat shows genuine creativity from the start, beginning with its distinct visual interpretation of its two worlds. The realm the Cat and his colleagues live in appears much more bright, colorful, and off-kilter compared to the more realistic and muted feel given to Gabby and Sebastian’s apartment life. The film thankfully provides solid laughs on a fairly frequent basis too, from sight gags and slapstick that can entertain all ages to some notably multilayered jokes that can easily work for kids but arguably hit harder for the adults in the audience.

It also certainly helps to have Bill Hader voicing the Cat, bringing his deft sense of humor to the role along with his ability to do impressive voices. In addition to Hader, the movie has a bit of a cheat code in the form of Matt Berry (What We Do in the Shadows) as the voice of Gabby and Sebastian's pet fish, Waffles, who the Cat promptly gives the ability to speak. Is there a greater and more innately funny voice than Berry's these days? Hearing his bombastic delivery as an overwhelmed and frustrated fish is continually funny.

The film’s storyline involves the Cat introducing and then promptly losing a device that functions in a manner similar to Doctor Strange's Time Stone, enabling the user to rewind recent events. The search for this device takes the Cat, Gabby, and Sebastian inside incredible versions of the moving boxes that still fill the kids’ apartment; they travel through worlds where everything inside these boxes appears larger than life, often having actually come to life in the form of various toys, objects, and drawings they encounter. While some of this is a bit reminiscent of the journey through the mind in Inside Out, there are a lot of unique and appreciated touches throughout as everything from musical instruments to IKEA instructions can and do express themselves in various ways.

The one big drawback with the film is that it’s simply too long for its subject matter, losing energy as it nears its conclusion. Running just a few minutes shy of two hours, it starts to drag in its third act; an obvious reason for this is that there are just too many overlapping conflicts introduced. The film is ultimately juggling the Cat’s quest to get back his lost device; a monstrous creature called “Something” who is pursuing our heroes; the fact that the Cat in the Hat's job is in jeopardy thanks to recent screw-ups; and another subplot about Carmen’s snooping landlord (Paula Pell), who is itching for a reason to evict the new family in the building thanks to her strict rules. It feels like Rivinoja and Carloni overcompensated for how slight the book is; the movie would have been better served by dropping at least one of these storylines, as the movie feels noticeably stretched out as it nears its resolution.

Still, despite overstaying its welcome, The Cat in the Hat remains easy to enjoy thanks to its likability and humor. That includes how it makes use of the book’s popular Thing 1 and Thing 2 characters, who are expanded here into a large group of similar Thing creatures that the Cat unleashes into Gabby and Sebastian’s apartment. These weird little guys have an amusing and wacky Gremlins-type chaotic energy, even as you can feel the studio salivating at the chance to turn the Things into the next Minions. But being aware of that is made easier when you’re watching an often sly film like The Cat in the Hat, which provides its own very good meta joke that acknowledges this fact with a wink.

articles.title: The New Disney+ K-Drama The Remarried Empress Takes Big Swings, But So Far Fails to Live Up to Its Full Potential
articles.summary: The Remarried Empress Episodes 1-4 review: The big-swing adaptation of the web novel has potential, but it's a rocky start.
articles.body:
This is a spoiler-light review of the first four episodes of The Remarried Empress, which are now available to stream on Disney+.

In the streaming wars, Disney has the obvious and not insignificant edge on princess stories. However, that edge tends to come in their kids/family content, which makes their biggest Korean drama swing yet — a big-budget romantasy epic called The Remarried Empress — kind of a brilliant programming decision. The 10-episode series is a live-action adaptation of a very popular web novel-turned-webtoon; the latter has accumulated almost three billion views on Naver. While technically the main character is an Empress and not a Princess, try telling that to her dresses, her gaggle of ladies-in-waiting, and her Beauty and the Beast-esque ballroom dance scene.

The Remarried Empress stars Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha's Shin Min-a as Navier, the elegant empress of the fictional Eastern Empire and wife to Emperor Sovieshu (The Trauma Code’s Ju Ji-hoon). Navier and Sovieshu share a respectful if not particularly passionate marriage, maintaining a stable royal leadership for the Eastern Empire. However, they have yet to have a child. When Sovieshu rescues escaped slave Rashta (The Red Sleeve’s Lee Se-young) from bounty hunters, he quickly falls for her, forcing Naiver to accept Rashta as an imperial mistress.

In a more stereotypical princess story, rags-to-riches Rashta would be the aspirational protagonist, and there’s a lot of potential in subverting that trope. However, The Remarried Empress does not live up to it, in large part due to the shallowness of its characters. The K-drama tries to give Navier more emotional interiority than her webtoon counterpart, but seems ultimately unwilling to stray too far from the source material characterization to make Navier particularly sympathetic in the first four episodes.

The result is a lead that is not particularly fun to root for. Though Navier may be beautiful and played by the likable Shin, it’s hard for a peasant like myself to care that the empress’ pride has been slighted and her commitment to the noble hierarchy upset. Perhaps another genre or a more masterful script could convince me to judge Emperor Sovieshu for his choice to chase love rather than duty, but The Remarried Empress is a romance, which means it needs viewers to believe that love is one of the most powerful forces of all and should be valued above most else. As the episodes progress, Sovieshu and Rashta become more and more like cartoon villains, securing a likability-by-comparison for Navier that is effective in building some sympathy.

Another potential path to establishing more gripping stakes would necessitate articulating the political stakes of disruption in the imperial marriage, or why Navier cares about having political power. However, at least in the first four episodes, it’s unclear what the Eastern Empire — or Navier — stands to suffer politically from the imperial divorce teased in the show’s title. The Remarried Empress premiere offers a peek at the fantastical danger in the kingdom when a massive worm-beast almost kills Navier while she and Sovieshu are out for a hunt. She is saved through her own skill and the help of enigmatic and handsome Prince Heinrey (Romance is a Bonus Book’s Lee Jong-suk), when he is in his secondary form as a bird; yes, a bird. These glimpses at magical world-building are intriguing, but don’t pay off in any cohesive way in the first act of the season.

The momentum suggested in the first episode does build when Prince Heinrey properly enters the narrative in his human form. In the first few episodes, he fosters a relationship with Navier solely as a bird, delivering messages to the empress from a mysterious admirer (i.e. him). In these encounters, the notorious ladies’ man begins to fall for the beautiful and lonely Navier. While Navier begins to see the bird as a confidante, she does not yet know that the creature she cares for and shares her secrets with is actually a human man, let alone the next in line for the throne of the Western Kingdom.

When Heinrey-as-human finally arrives at the Eastern Empire court, along with nobility from other empires for a New Year’s Celebration, The Remarried Empress utilizes some killer historical-romance-on-screen shorthands to great effect. When Navier and Heinrey share a dance in a ballroom of their royal social circle, it builds on the cinematic language crafted by Pride and Prejudice adaptations and recently utilized by Bridgerton to instantly communicate authentic, romantic intimacy. More broadly, the charismatic irreverence of Prince Heinrey’s character brings a much-needed levity to the self-serious triangle of Navier, Sovieshu, and Rashta, and his instant devotion to Navier gives us something more substantial to root for.

The interplay between these four main characters is helped immensely by the quality of this cast and by the lavish production design and setting. The Remarried Empress seemingly spared no expense in bringing the fantasy romance to the screen. Unlike most Korean historical fantasy dramas, Remarried Empress' palace setting is inspired by European architecture, fashion, and etiquette, and was filmed in the Czech Republic and Germany to capture a Western aesthetic. This blend of a Western-inspired fantasy setting with a Korean cast and story sensibility gives The Remarried Empress a unique watchability, even if it doesn’t have anything particularly interesting to say about power or politics thus far.

The Remarried Empress also benefits greatly from the current dearth of big-budget romantasy series. Despite the massive success of book series like A Court of Thorns and Roses, we have gotten so few big-budget TV shows in the genre, which speaks to Hollywood’s broader devaluing of romance-centric storytelling over the past few decades and women as our own audience. While this is beginning to change in no small part due to the massive, proven success of Korean dramas around the world, we have yet to see a breakout hit. Netflix’s Shadow and Bone had immense potential, but was canceled (despite its strong viewership) before getting to the main Six of Crows storyline, widely considered to be the meatiest part of Leigh Bardugo’s Grishaverse; I still lament.

So far, The Remarried Empress is nowhere near as good as Six of Crows, though it might be on par with Shadow and Bone; I hope it gets a chance to evolve in a way the Shadow and Bone adaptation never did. In a global streaming landscape that takes so few big swings on romantasy series, we can’t be too hasty about dismissing a series like The Remarried Empress. In its first four episodes, it has yet to live up to the potential of the immense creative and financial resources invested in it, but what’s a princess story for if not believing in a happier ending?

articles.title: Judi Dench Reveals Daniel Craig Pushed to Kill Off M in Skyfall
articles.summary: Dame Judi Dench, who portrayed 007’s boss M in eight James Bond films over 20 years, claims (somewhat tongue-in-cheek) that Daniel Craig was responsible for having her character die in 2012’s Skyfall.
articles.body:
Dame Judi Dench, who portrayed 007’s boss M in eight James Bond films over 20 years, claims that Daniel Craig was responsible for having her character die in 2012’s Skyfall .

Variety published an excerpt from Dench’s new memoir, Is It Too Late to Make a Run For It?, wherein the Oscar winner recalled how she found out that M was going to be killed off.

“I was taken to the Wolseley restaurant by Barbara, Michael and Sam [Mendes, the director] – I don’t think Daniel Craig was there – and they outlined the plot and told me they were going to bump me off. My own fault, I suppose,” Dench said, in a somewhat tongue-in-cheek manner . “Ever since GoldenEye , when the entire film unit went off to Monte Carlo and St. Petersburg and I only had three days in Watford, I’d been begging them to let me out from behind my desk. Well, they did finally let me out from behind my desk … and they shot me.”

Dench – who first played the role in 1995’s GoldenEye opposite Pierce Brosnan in his debut as James Bond – then named who decided it was time for her M to finally get the ax. (Dench’s M did make a posthumous cameo in Spectre .)

“Apparently, it was Daniel’s idea to have me killed. But first I had to suffer the indignity of being sacked by Ralph Fiennes. Arsehole [ laughs ],” Dench said.

Dench also revealed that 1997’s Tomorrow Never Dies was the most difficult Bond film to make, citing “a general air of chaos” that consumed the production.

“Making a film is nerve-racking enough – at least it is for me – and to be presented with a load of rewrites last minute is very destabilizing: there are whole new chunks of information to take in – not to mention new lines to learn – that you haven’t had the time to examine,” Dench said.

“Every day we’d be presented with new scenes. On one occasion I arrived home at 10 o’clock at night only to be greeted by a motorcycle courier with a dozen new pages to be learnt before my pick-up at 5am the following morning. I mean, when the hell would I have a chance to learn all that? It’s not unusual to have rewrites on a film, but the script for Tomorrow Never Dies seemed to be in a permanent state of flux.”

In related news, new Bond studio Amazon MGM Studios’ search for the next actor to play James Bond is coming down to the wire, with Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, and Josh O’Connor reportedly the frontrunners to succeed Daniel Craig.

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

articles.title: Police Mock Car Chase Criminal for Getting Arrested Right Before GTA 6 Release
articles.summary: Police in Derbyshire, UK, are going viral after making a TikTok video mocking a criminal who led them on a high-speed car chase, saying the suspect will now miss out on GTA 6’s highly-anticipated launch as a consequence of their actions.
articles.body:
Police in Derbyshire, UK, are going viral after making a TikTok video mocking a criminal who led them on a car chase, saying the suspect will now miss out on GTA 6’s highly-anticipated launch as a consequence of their actions.

The short video, uploaded to TikTok on November 3, shows law enforcement officers from the Derbyshire county constabulary chasing a black van through residential streets as the song ‘Flower in a Hurricane’ from the GTA 6 soundtrack plays.

The video leaned into the Grand Theft Auto series aesthetic; whoever edited the clip put GTA 6’s unmistakable UI over top, giving the criminal a three-star rating, and even included a minimap in the corner of the screen that followed his bungled escape. Eventually, police were able to cut him off and make an arrest.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

According to the post’s caption, the incident took place in the town of Ripley. The suspect, 28-year-old Jack Vickrage, has been sentenced to 14 months in prison for “admitting dangerous driving, driving while disqualified, drug-driving, and cannabis possession.”

“Could've just waited a few more weeks for GTA 6 to drop... Now Jack's in prison for release day," the constabulary captioned its post. "Thirteen years is a long time to wait for the game, but nothing excuses driving like this in real life. Cutting corners and hurtling through residential streets with pedestrians and other vehicles in the middle of the day... save that stuff for the streets of Vice City.”

Commenters were thoroughly impressed by the short video, urging the department to “give the admin early access [to GTA 6]” and saying the “admin needs a raise.”

“15 more days to go, he can watch us play from prison,” another joked.

GTA 6 launches on November 19. Just this morning, Rockstar confirmed the game’s install size and global release times , saying the preload file can measure up to 212 GB depending on your device. “Make sure you've got ample space to begin pre-loading as soon as possible,” the developer said.

It’s shaping up to be one of the biggest pop culture events in history, with Rockstar going all-out on marketing; they partnered with Miami, Florida for a Vice City-themed takeover and collaborated with the Miami Heat to give them special, GTA 6-themed jerseys . Xbox even debuted an alligator-shaped Xbox Series X today in keeping with the game’s Florida setting, which players can win if they enter a sweepstakes. (And no, it’s not a real alligator.)

There’s just two more weeks until GTA 6 is finally in players’ hands; in the meantime, oodles of fans have made plans to take off work to play it , while others are planning to call out sick on the day. Others are so amped about it that they even said they would abandon their pets for a month if they had the chance to play it early in a recent survey.

articles.title: Netflix Calls Its New AI Discover Feature a 'Test Kitchen' to Tailor Viewers' Recommendations
articles.summary: Netflix is rolling out a new AI-powered feature with the aim of helping viewers pick what to watch when they can’t decide.
articles.body:
Netflix is rolling out a new AI-powered feature with the aim of helping viewers pick what to watch when they can’t decide.

We’ve all been there; like Clueless’s Cher looking into her closet and exclaiming in dismay that there’s simply "nothing to wear," there are certainly times when it seems like streaming services have lots of shows and movies on offer, but nothing that’s appealing in the immediate moment.

Netflix is attempting to help with this conundrum with its latest tool, titled AI Discover. Announced on November 3, it sits on the top bar of the TV app on the far right. Open it up, and Netflix’s AI will conjure up a few themes to choose from.

The streamer’s example of this includes themes like Outsmart Everyone, Family Scandal Sagas, and Royal Court Intrigue. As told in an explainer on Netflix’s website , some of these themes match “how you want to feel,” the people you’re watching with, or how much time you have, while others are based around your recent watch history or more popular trending picks.

After choosing one of these themes, Netflix’s AI will bring up similar recommendations, presenting more specific themes until the perfect show or movie arises. And if you’re simply not finding anything interesting, you can refresh your search by choosing ‘Something Different.’

Similar to Netflix’s My List option, you can also hit a ‘Tune Your Recommendations’ button, which sits next to your list and Play. This will let you save a recommendation from the AI, or tell it not to recommend a show you aren’t interested in seeing.

In an official statement, Netflix described the tool as its “test kitchen,” saying that it’s “trying out new recipes for discovery, and your use and feedback help us decide which ones to keep, improve, or serve up next. Some may even make their way into the main Netflix experience.”

“What we’re most excited about is how it feels to use,” the statement continues. “Tell us what you’re after, and the experience adjusts. Tell us a recommendation isn’t for you, and we’ll remember it in AI Discover, so it won’t keep turning up. AI Discover is powered by a new intelligence layer we’ve been building that responds to what members tell us in real time and keeps learning.”

AI Discover is rolling out to US-based members who use the service in English on supported TVs, and will gradually release for more users over the coming weeks.

Netflix is the latest of several major streaming services and entertainment platforms to add AI features in its product; Spotify went so far as to introduce AI DJs that will mix music for you , while Roku infamously added a 24/7 AI channel with series that are totally generated with artificial intelligence. Netflix, for its part, simply wants to better tailor viewers’ recommendations, though we’ll see what the public sentiment ends up looking like as more subscribers use it.

articles.title: What PS5 and Xbox Consoles Are in Stock Ahead of GTA 6 and Black Friday?
articles.summary: Sony and Microsoft are warning about console shortages ahead of GTA 6 and Black Friday. Which consoles are available (or not) right now?
articles.body:
With both Black Friday and the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 around the corner, console shortages have been in the news lately.

Xbox head Asha Sharma recently said there’s more demand than Xbox consoles available , and Microsoft told told Xbox owners to trade in their dusty consoles . Meanwhile, over on the other side of the aisle, Sony wants to buy your PS5 for $400 , and anyone in the market for a PS5 Pro may have to shell out as much as $1,400 to a reseller to get one.

Console stock must be getting pretty dire, right? To answer that question, I visited all the major online retailers to see what the status is surrounding console availability. And what I found was, with the exception of the PS5 Pro, every current model of every current console is widely available at manufacturer-suggested retail price (MSRP).

Xbox Series X (1TB All-Digital Edition - Robot White)

Now, that doesn't mean that's how things will stay as GTA 6 and Black Friday creep nearer. And it's worth noting that those MSRPs have gone up in recent years. But at least at this pre-Black Friday, pre-GTA 6 moment in time, it’s not hard to find a new game console at retail price – unless you want a PS5 Pro. Let’s take a look at where things stand with every current model of every game console.

To kick things off, yes, new PlayStation 5 Pro consoles are sold out everywhere. You can still get a used one at eBay or marked up by third-party retailers at some of the links above, but they cost around $1,500, so buy at your own risk. Moving on…

Even though Sony is doing away with discs starting in January 2028 , the PlayStation company will still happily sell you a PS5 with a disc drive. This model of the PS5 is widely available pretty much everywhere, so pick one up at your favorite retailer. It's unlikely these consoles will get discounts during P layStation's Black Friday sale this year .

As you may have heard (in the previous blurb), Sony is doing away with discs starting in January 2028. If you’re ready to embrace that digital-only life, feel free to grab this one. At $599.99, it’s pretty much a steal in this (horrible) economy. However, it's worth noting that Amazon and GameStop are currently sold out of new stock of this model, while other retailers have it in stock.

The standard Xbox Series X with a disc drive is available at most retailers. It's worth noting that both Target and Microsoft are currently sold out, which could be what Sharma was referring to in her comments about supply not being able to keep up with demand.

We’ve seen a lot of evidence over the years suggesting Xbox console sales are lagging badly behind PS5. The most recent hint that this is the case came from Capcom, which says only 8.6% of Resident Evil Requiem sales were on Xbox . But if you’re willing to throw in with Microsoft anyway, you can get an Xbox Series X at MSRP at most of the usual retailers, with the exception of Xbox directly.

The slightly less powerful Xbox Series S is available in two models that are identical in all ways except the amount of storage that comes in them.

The same goes for the digital-only (and less powerful) Xbox Series S. It’s available at MSRP pretty much everywhere consoles are sold.

Nintendo seems to have plenty of Switch 2 consoles on hand, but if you’re curious about how much it costs and where to get it, you can check out the links above. Like PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, it’s widely available at MSRP.

With all that said, if you’re considering picking a new game console this holiday season, you may want to do it sooner rather than later. It’s absolutely quite possible that Sony and Microsoft are simply looking ahead at the Black Friday sales rush when issuing their warnings about stock. It’s possible a bunch of GTA 6 fans will rush out to get a console when the game launches on November 19 (preloads start November 10, by the way).

And it’s looking like RAMageddon will only get worse in 2027 , meaning we could see further console shortages or price increases in the near future. So grab a console if you need it, because they’re readily available at the time of this writing.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Notre-Dame - Finding the Shadow Walkthrough - Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This is a continuation of IGN's walkthrough for Castlevania: Belmont's Curse. In this section, we'll be focusing on the Notre-Dame section, an
articles.body:
This is a continuation of IGN's walkthrough for Castlevania: Belmont's Curse . In this section, we'll be focusing on the Notre-Dame section, an area you can unlock after defeating the Occultist , Carmilla, and obtaining the Paintbrush from her, which she stole from the Artist . You need to complete the Library to unlock this section and add the Artist to your Tarot cards, whom you can unlock after defeating the Builder in the Clock Tower . You can follow along with this playthrough to review the previous sections here.

We'll be starting this walkthrough at the entrance of the Notre-Dame painting. You can find it in the Main Hall.

From this starting point, head to the right and make your way into the next room. Although there is a pair of knights here, these 'statues' won't move yet. You'll be free to access the glowing door on the right side of the room and advance into the Nave.

Here, you'll encounter a new type of trap. You'll see glowing green runes hanging underneath the spike platforms throughout the room. The glowing rune is a symbol for a musical note, specifically F clef. Expect to see more of these musical notes and symbols throughout your time exploring Notre-Dame, as they're important to the greater mystery in this part of Belmont's Curse. For now, avoid these blasts as they're fired out, and expect to discover more of them as you advance. There are also a pair of knights in this hallway that you'll need to defeat, and one of them is a new type of knight.

This knight has a large shield with a dragon on it. It's similar to the knights with the handaxes. Only it uses the shield to protect itself from your attacks if the shield is facing you. Otherwise, it takes damage normally. Also, if you attempt to use your whip attack on it while its shield is facing you, the end won't attach, and you won't be able to rush toward it.

Once these two knights are defeated, make your way to the right side of the room to advance forward. In the next hallway, you'll find even more runes with the F Clef on them, as they fire out blasts in your pathway. This area is quick to clear as you head through the next glowing doorway.

This brings you to the Transept, where a trio of different colored runes is blocking your path forward. The first is the F Clef, the second is an Octave Clef, and the third is the Tenor Clef. You cannot bypass these blasts right now, unfortunately. The only path for you to explore is to go through the glowing section at the entrance and head below.

You'll discover the Notre-Dame Undercroft in this portion, with more runes in your path forward. Continue below, fighting off the floating skulls that appear along the way. When you reach the bottom, there's a doorway to your right that leads to the Mirror of Life for this area. Head inside to activate it, providing you with a suitable place to set a checkpoint should you die or need to fast travel elsewhere.

After unlocking this checkpoint, return to the room you were just in in the Undercroft. Unfortunately, you can't go through the doors on the left side, as they're blocked by the runes with the beams. However, you can follow the grate down.

Take it, and you'll make your way to the Great Organ Room. When you reach this bottom level, use your Talos Smash by jumping into the air and then slamming down by using your jump button to break through the wall.

This will take you to the proper Great Organ Room, where you'll land on one of the organ tiles. Each tile plays a specific note, with the three Clef symbols in the back that match the rune traps you found when you initially arrived in Notre-Dame. There are three rows of runes with the F Clef patterns on them, preventing you from moving forward to the right, forcing you to follow down the left path.

You won't have to go far. When you reach the end of this path, there's a wall that you can break to find a hidden area. In this hidden area is an interactable in the middle that reads, "Beneath these stairs lies our order's greatest sin." It's a hint that you can find something under the stairs, but it does not share how you get to it. The spirit at the end of the dead end, though, is much more important.

They have a Clue for you surrounding the Shadow that says you must find the melodies of the Music Masters of Notre-Dame to clear the corruption. It provides you with the first melody sheet, which you're going to need.

Head back to the Great Organ Room and play out the pattern you found on the melody sheet. You'll be able to do this by hitting them in the correct order. There are 14 different notes on this organ. Numbering them left to right, hit notes 8, 7, 8 again, 6, and then 5 .

You'll know you've done this correctly when the F Clef organ in the blast disappears, and the glowing symbols to your right lower, allowing you to proceed to the next area. Make your way to the right, and you'll enter the Collapsed Crypt.

You'll encounter a pair of archers, a gargoyle, and a consistently respawning floating skull in this room. After dispatching them, make your way up the platform and open the door. Advance through the hallway, and you'll have a choice to go up or further to the right.

Before going to the right, take the path up, and you'll proceed to the Path of the Penitent. Use your wall-leap to reach the top, and open the door leading to the pathway on the left. You'll connect the Notre-Dame Undercroft Mirror of Life with this path, allowing you to quickly retrace your steps without taking any alternative routes.

Once you bridge this connection, head back down to the Collapsed Crypt and follow the path to the right. However, before doing this, drop down to the first breakable platform and slide to the left. There's a small gap that you can slip through where you'll find a Spirit waiting for you. Speak with the Spirit, and you'll acquire another clue surrounding the Shadow. The Spirit reveals where the Music Masters fled to escape Death.

You can then take the small path to the left and retrace your steps to proceed to the left. Now, there is a series of breakable platforms that you have to cross before you swing to the right, using the yellow anchor in the room. You'll need to dodge the Tenor Clif runes blasting energy while you do this.

After you swing to the right, there's another breakable platform that you have to reach. However, there's also another Tenor Clif rune blasting down from the top, likely preventing you from passing. If you can't go by immediately, use the purple anchor above you to hold this place without falling into the spike pit, and wait for the energy to disappear. You may need to use the Air Dash to reach the other side and the next glowing door. Beware the floating skulls as they appear during this platforming bit!

This next section will take you to the Chapel of Patience. Proceed to the right, and you'll face off against a pair of knights with lances, next to an interactable stone. Read the stone that reads, "Patiens Qvia Aeternvs. Patience is the mother of all Virtue."

As you advance down to the end of this path, unfortunately, you won't be able to go past them because the Octave and Tenor runes are still active. You'll need to complete the two other Music Master melodies to proceed through here.

However, you can go above and use the top section, breaking the runed floor, allow you to bypass the middle section the next time you return.

For now, head up to the top of Chapel of Patience. When you reach the top, there's a section that breaks off, above a lever. Head down and hit the lever, where a pair of knights with dragon shields come to life.

After taking them out, head through the door on the left, and you'll have unlocked a passage with a Relic chest on the far left.

Unlock the chest, and you'll receive Beelzebub's Seal ( Rose deals 30% more damage, but her maximum life is reduced by 50% ).

You can now return to the upper right side that you were taking in the Chapel of Patience, and proceed to the area, bringing you to a section of the Path o the Penitent.

There are a handful of initial enemies for you to fight in this room. You can make short work of them, and there's a lever above you, but you won't be able to access it right now. You can, however, proceed to the left path, which is a tricky puzzle that you have to complete in a limited time (if you want to unlock the weapon).

On the far left side is a trio of beams that fire down the entire hallway. You'll need to wait until they initially fire, and then head down. You'll want to pause at the small gap on the lower section for the beams to fire again (they'll shoot harmlessly above you), before jumping up and reaching the area with the lever.

Now, when you hit the lever, the timer starts. You want to wait until the beams have activated and have gone for a few seconds. Hitting the lever right before they shut off should give you the most amount of time to advance. You can always restart the timer by hitting the lever again. Thankfully, you do respawn right at the lever, but if it's still going when you respawn, I recommend hitting it to reset it and trying again.

When the timer begins, jump down and dive to the section next to the stairs. Crouch down and hold it there, waiting for the beams to fire. When they finish, slide forward and jump up to the top area. Hold on the sides of the wall for the beams to fire, shut off, and then you can proceed forward. Jump through the spikes using your air dash.

When you're through, there will be an area with the abyss shards. You can stand here without taking a hit. Wait for the trio of beams to fire and then shut off before jumping and activating your Halo to pass through.

After making it through the shards, there's a purple anchor above you that you can use, and then slam down onto the breakable floor beneath you, reaching the bottom, where you'll find the weapon chest. You'll be able to unlock the Joyeuse longsword.

You can then make the climb back up to where you smashed through the rocks (potentially grabbing the XP statue in front of where the beams are shooting), and head to the left. Going down this path has you coming across a handful of enemies before you find another smashable ground piece. Use the purple anchor above it to give yourself enough room, and then slam down, bringing you back down the same path you took from the Collapsed Crypt. You want to return to the Notre-Dame Undercroft Mirror of Life.

From there, take the left path and go through the glowing door on the left side, bringing you to the Way of the Confessor.

On this path, you'll need to make your way up (dodging the blasts from the runes) as you reach the top. Unfortunately, the top glowing door is not a viable path right now, forcing you to continue your way down. You'll need to jump down onto the breakable platform, and then air dash across the middle to reach the second breakable platform. From there, jump to the top to reach the other side.

The timing can be tricky here. I recommend dropping down shortly after the side runes fire, allowing you to reach the platform and jump into the air. You should have enough time to air dash across the gap without being hit. It's not the end if you are, but you do start over from this spot if you hit the spikes.

After that, in the next room you'll be ambushed by multiple undead, namely the ranged undead, and a pair of knights, with a large sphere with faces shooting at you. You won't be able to wait for the rune beams in the center to end. Instead, you have to drop down from the grates, air dash above the spikes, and then use the purple anchor to reach the other side. Expect to have to do that often for this fight.

Once you clear this area, proceed to the left and jump across the breakable platforms to the far left side.

Through the glowing door, you'll reach the Tomb of the Chevaliers, underneath the entrance to Notre-Dame you took from the Main Hall.

From this section, you'll be able to use a yellow anchor to swing to the upper part. However, after using the yellow anchor, you might notice it begins to pull down when you use it. If you go back and forth, swinging from it left to right, it begins to lower and eventually opens the path on the bottom left side.

When taking this route, you'll jump from the initial platform and use the purple anchor to launch yourself to the left side (you may need to air dash to cross the spikes). Here, you'll land on a breakable platform. There are three of these platforms on the bottom section, not giving you too much time to remain down here.

You need to wait for the beam to stop firing on the left side so you can grab the purple anchor and swing yourself up. You then need to wait for the beam on the right side to stop firing so you can dash forward, and complete this puzzle.

When you reach the other side, you'll find a Permanent Attack boost, and you can slide beneath the wall on the right side to fight against the skeleton ogre and the undead archer on the upper platform.

Upon defeating this pair of enemies, head to the upper left side (however, you can go through the abyss shards at the top of the room using the yellow anchors to find a pair of XP statues in this area before advancing).

Follow this path up to the top, and you'll return to the left side of the Narthex, your initial starting point in Notre-Dame. However, you're on the left side of this area, and there's a massive crow in the middle of the room. Defeat it, and you can hit the pressure plate on the right side of the wall, opening your path to the left. Before going too far, though, make sure to break the door down at the bottom of this room to connect it to the Notre-Dame painting entrance.

This upper pathway brings you to the Tower Entrance.

The RTX 5070 Ti is our best reviewed Blackwell card because it offers the best bang for your buck in terms of 4K gaming performance. It performs neck-and-neck with the previous generation RTX 4080 Super and pulls ahead in any game that supports multi-frame generation, especially with the DLSS 4.5 update .

It is fully capable of running any game in 4K at 60fps, including Death Stranding 2 and Crimson Desert . The RTX 5070 Ti also comes equipped with 16GB of VRAM like the RTX 5080, making it viable for AI work. Since this GPU is impossible to find as a standalone card for under $999.99, buying a prebuilt computer is the only way to avoid a markup.

articles.title: Play-Doh Reveals Its First Romantasy Crossover for ACOTAR Fans
articles.body:
The new A Court of Thorns and Roses book was just released last week and there's already been a ton of new merchandise attached to it. There's plushies, puzzles, necklaces, and even board games now available for ACOTAR fans in 2026. And now even Play-Doh is getting in on the romantasy bandwagon with a new Blooms bouquet kit.

The Play-Doh Blooms A Court of Throns and Roses kit is up for preorder now at Amazon for $49.99 and will release on January 15, 2026. The kit includes a book vase and a Truth-teller dagger.

Play-Doh Blooms A Court of Thorns and Roses

If you're wondering why Play-Doh is suddenly making kids for adults, the answer is pretty simple: Adults are buying more toys than ever. Hasbro announced the new line of adult-focused Play-Doh back in July .

“The Play-Doh brand has always been about the limitless possibilities of imagination. That feeling doesn’t fade as you grow up, it evolves,” said Brian Baker, Senior Vice President at Hasbro. “ Blooms by Play-Doh serves that need, offering a more elevated, hands-on way to slow down, get lost in the process and create something beautiful you can enjoy long after you’ve made it."

The idea of adult-focused flower kits isn't new. LEGO has had its very successful Botanicals line of builds for years now and they are consistently some of the most popular sets for adults . The Play-Doh version of this concept is a little less straightforward than a package of bricks, but offers a softer look that looks a bit more organic up close.

The new Play-Doh set will arrive just a few days after the release of book seven, A Court of Forgotten Melody. Sarah J. Maas has hinted that a book eight is on the way as well, though no release date has been set.
